finding_ec2_idle.observed: Average CPU was 1.2% over 7 days (168 of 168 hourly datapoints).
finding_ec2_idle.why: Running instances are billed every hour, even when they do very little.
finding_ec2_idle.next_step: Check with whoever owns it. If it's not needed, stop it, or move it to a smaller type.
limitations: Low CPU doesn't prove it's unused. It might be busy on memory, network, or rare jobs.
Stopping it keeps the EBS volumes, and those are still billed.

finding_s3_incomplete_uploads.observed: 3 incomplete uploads older than 7 days, the oldest started 2026-09-02.
finding_s3_incomplete_uploads.why: Parts of unfinished uploads are stored and billed, but don't show up as objects.
finding_s3_incomplete_uploads.next_step: Add a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete uploads after 7 days.
limitations: We don't know how much data the parts hold, so there's no savings number.

finding_s3_tiering.observed: 383.7 GiB across 48,210 objects in S3 Standard, with no transition rules.
finding_s3_tiering.why: Standard is the most expensive storage class for data that's rarely read.
finding_s3_tiering.next_step: Move objects into Intelligent-Tiering, which moves them to cheaper tiers when they aren't read.
limitations: We can't see how often objects are read, so the benefit is unknown.
finding_s3_tiering.charges: Small monitoring fee per object, plus a one-time transition request charge.
